clue.text: Mark one of the cards — a club

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for mark, the old German currency
an ace is one of the playing cards in a pack

explanation.surface: A card player marks one card in the pack, a club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a club' looks like part of the card talk, the suit of clubs, but it is the definition: a heavy club used as a weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: A mace is a heavy spiked club carried as a weapon or ceremonial staff.

clue.text: Official letter from American state I have received

parts.note: Miss is the abbreviation for Mississippi
I've is the contraction of I have

explanation.surface: A formal letter from America that I have been sent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'received' merely says the letter arrived, joining the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A missive is a letter, especially a long or formal one.

clue.text: Matches scheduled, including this game

indicators.note: including means the letters are contained within the words that precede it

explanation.surface: The fixture list includes games of this kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Chess is a board game, played in matches at tournaments.

clue.text: Two-way broadcaster

indicators.note: a word that runs two ways reads the same forwards and backwards, so the whole entry is a palindrome

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A broadcaster that transmits both ways.
explanation.walkthrough: The BEEB is the British nickname for the BBC; the four letters read the same in either direction.
explanation.definitionFit: The Beeb is the familiar British nickname for the BBC, the national public broadcaster.

clue.text: Insect with two things on head

parts.note: an ear is found on the head
a wig is worn on the head

explanation.surface: A bug with a pair of antennae on top.
explanation.definitionFit: The earwig is a small insect with pincers at the tail.

clue.text: Having some problem in seeing manager, I'd heard

parts.note: a boss is a manager

indicators.note: heard means the word is listened to, so it gives letters that sound the same

parts.note: said aloud, these words sound like EYED

explanation.surface: Someone tells the manager they have an eyesight problem.
explanation.walkthrough: BOSS-EYED is British for having a squint.
explanation.definitionFit: Boss-eyed is British slang for squinting or cross-eyed, a defect of vision.

clue.text: Wine casks blown up in Scotland

definitions.meaning: a pipe is a large cask for wine, especially port
the bagpipes, played by blowing into the bag, are Scotland's instrument

explanation.surface: Barrels of wine exploded somewhere in Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blown up' suggests an explosion, but it means air blown into the bagpipes, the instrument associated with Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: A pipe is a large barrel for wine, and the pipes are bagpipes, played by blowing.

clue.text: Theatre work for ugly, prim, unmarried actress in new production

indicators.note: a new production of a play remakes it, so these letters are rearranged
M is the abbreviation for married, so 'unmarried' tells us to drop that letter from prim

explanation.surface: A plain, prudish single actress gets cast in a fresh staging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Theatre' is the operating theatre, not the stage. PRIM loses M, leaving PRI, which with UGLY and ACTRESS is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Plastic surgery is work done in an operating theatre to reshape the body.

clue.text: She accepts the daily round

parts.note: reads like someone resigned to routine, but it is a girl taking on a delivery round of daily newspapers

explanation.definitionFit: A girl who delivers newspapers on a daily round to homes.

clue.text: Build defence for French authoress over case

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means placed above, so the author's name comes first

parts.note: George Sand was the pen name of a French woman novelist
a bag is a case for carrying things

explanation.surface: A French novelist's suitcase sits on top of her defences.
explanation.definitionFit: To sandbag a position is to fortify it with bags of sand against flood or fire.

clue.text: One could get nice tip, perhaps, from this form of instruction

indicators.note: says the letters could be rearranged to get the phrase that follows, so this is an anagram

explanation.surface: An apprentice might earn a decent tip during this training.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of NICE TIP PERHAPS rearrange into the answer; 'from this' signals the answer is the source of the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: An apprenticeship is training in a trade under a skilled master.

clue.text: Mole sheds skin again, rejecting it

indicators.note: rejecting the assembled word means turning it back, so the letters are read in reverse order

parts.note: to peel is to shed skin, as after sunburn
re- is the prefix meaning again

explanation.surface: A small burrowing mole moults its skin once more and refuses it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mole' looks like the animal, which fits shedding skin, but it is a spy. 'rejecting it' turns each piece round where it stands: PEELS to SLEEP and RE to ER.
explanation.definitionFit: In spy jargon a sleeper is an agent planted long in advance, as a mole is.

clue.text: Nurse inserting instrument to make a point

indicators.note: the nurse is shown taking something in, so the instrument goes inside her letters

parts.note: SEN is State Enrolled Nurse, a former British nursing grade
the harp is a stringed musical instrument

explanation.surface: A nurse puts an instrument in place to prove a point.
explanation.walkthrough: SEN (State Enrolled Nurse) was a British nursing qualification.
explanation.definitionFit: To sharpen something is to give it a fine point, as with a pencil.

clue.text: Type of training that's not ruled out of court?

definitions.meaning: training given to staff while they stay employed in their jobs

definitions.text: that's not ruled out of court?
definitions.meaning: in tennis a serve that lands in court is good, not ruled out

explanation.surface: A form of training that a judge would not throw out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of court' suggests a law court; it is a tennis court, where a serve called in is not ruled out.
explanation.definitionFit: In-service training is given to employees during their working life; a serve landing inside the lines is in.

clue.text: Pulse cooked in broth

indicators.note: cooked suggests something prepared and altered, so the letters of broth are rearranged

explanation.surface: Lentils or beans cooked in a soup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pulse' looks like the lentils that would go in broth, but it is a heartbeat.
explanation.definitionFit: A throb is a strong regular beat, like the pulse of the heart.

clue.text: Employ editor to restrain Times writer

indicators.note: restraining means holding something in, so the editor's letters go round the rest

parts.note: X is the multiplication sign, read as times
a pen is a writing instrument

explanation.surface: Hire an editor to keep a Times journalist in check.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' looks like the newspaper, but it is the multiplication sign X.
explanation.definitionFit: To expend is to use up or spend, as one may employ resources.

clue.text: Behave like a champion when points are lost

definitions.text: Behave like a champion when points are lost

parts.words: Behave like a champion when points are lost
parts.note: a champion can mean a supporter or backer, and a sponsor who props up a losing side acts as one; the verb also suggests talking down to the loser

explanation.walkthrough: A champion is a supporter, so to behave like one is to act as a backer of someone; the second sense, to be condescending, fits a victor towards a loser.
explanation.definitionFit: To act as a patron is to support or sponsor; the word also means to treat with condescension.

clue.text: Attractive female making an impression

parts.note: an etching is a print, an impression taken from an etched plate

explanation.surface: A pretty woman leaves her mark on people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making an impression' sounds like charm, but an impression is a print taken from a plate.
explanation.definitionFit: Fetching is an informal synonym for attractive or charming.

clue.text: Study deceptive appearance of face

parts.note: to con is an old word for to study or learn
a front is a false outward show

explanation.surface: Examine the misleading look of someone's features.
explanation.definitionFit: To confront is to face up to someone or something directly.

clue.text: Act trickily in case, getting it held over in particular confusion

indicators.note: something held is kept inside, so the turned word sits within the outer letters

parts.note: a pet subject is one's particular favourite
fog is a state of mental confusion

indicators.note: turned over, so the word it is read backwards

explanation.surface: A lawyer plays tricks in a case, with the matter adjourned amid confusion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Act trickily in case' is the definition: the case is a lawsuit, and pettifogging is a petty lawyer's quibbling. 'held over' suggests an adjourned hearing, but 'over' turns IT round and 'held' sets it inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To pettifog is to quibble over trivial legal points, the chicanery of a petty lawyer.

clue.text: Support given to the extraordinarily inspired teacher

parts.note: a prop is a support

indicators.note: something done extraordinarily is out of its ordinary order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Help offered to the remarkably gifted schoolmaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extraordinarily' rearranges THE to HET.
explanation.definitionFit: A prophet is a divinely inspired teacher or messenger.

clue.text: Familiar difficulty when turning back cloth

indicators.note: turning back means the joined words are read in reverse order

parts.note: a pal is a friend, someone familiar
the rub is the difficulty, as in Hamlet's 'there's the rub'

explanation.surface: A family problem arises when someone returns a piece of fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Burlap is a coarse woven fabric of jute or hemp, used for sacking.

clue.text: Describe wine that goes with fish

parts.note: port is a fortified wine from Portugal
the ray is a flat fish

explanation.surface: Tell us which wine goes with the fish course.
explanation.definitionFit: To portray is to depict or represent in words or pictures.

clue.text: Chap, half-cut during dance, upset Casanova

indicators.note: during places one thing in the middle of another, so the half word goes inside
in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the dance's letters are reversed

parts.note: a reel is a lively Scottish folk dance

indicators.note: cut in half, so only the first two letters of chap are kept

explanation.surface: A tipsy man at a dance gets upset with a famous womaniser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-cut' reads as drunk, but it signals half the word chap; 'upset' turns the dance round to LEER, and 'during' sets the half word inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Casanova, the Venetian adventurer, is a byword for a womaniser, a lecherous man.

clue.text: Australian cricket side found English air fresh and bracing

parts.note: Oz is informal for Australia or Australian
the on side is the leg side of a cricket field

explanation.surface: Touring Australian cricketers found the English air invigorating.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the field divides into the off side and the on (leg) side, which gives ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Ozone is used informally for fresh, invigorating air, especially at the seaside.

clue.text: Merchant vessel about to be surrounded by hostile aircraft

indicators.note: something surrounded is enclosed, so the short word goes inside the aircraft

parts.note: a fighter is a warplane used to attack enemy aircraft
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A merchant ship is about to be encircled by enemy planes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about to be' reads as 'on the point of', but 'about' is RE and 'to be surrounded by' the insertion signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A freighter is a ship carrying cargo, a merchant vessel rather than a warship.

clue.text: "Drink like a fish" about right as example of this?

definitions.text: "Drink like a fish" about right as example of this?

indicators.note: about means going round, so the drinking word goes round the letter for right

parts.note: to tope is to drink alcohol heavily

explanation.surface: Is the saying about heavy drinking a fair figure of speech?
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'drink like a fish' is itself a figure of speech, so the whole clue defines the answer as well as building it.
explanation.definitionFit: A trope is a figure of speech; the simile in quotes is an example of one.

clue.text: Expression of resignation finding grass with weed, say

indicators.note: say signals that the words are to be spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: hay is dried grass and to hoe is to weed

explanation.surface: A gardener sighs on finding grass full of weeds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'weed' is a verb here: to hoe.
explanation.definitionFit: Heigh-ho is an exclamation of weary acceptance or mild boredom.

clue.text: Nurse takes some time over withdrawing support

indicators.note: the time takes something in, so the turned support goes inside it

parts.note: an hour is a span of time

indicators.note: withdrawing suggests drawing back, so the word support gives is read backwards

parts.note: a bra is a supporting undergarment

explanation.surface: A nurse spends time over removing a patient's support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nurse' here is a verb, as in nursing a grudge.
explanation.definitionFit: To harbour a feeling is to nurse it, keeping it alive in the mind.

clue.text: Association football match has ended

parts.note: a tie is a cup match between two teams
up means over or finished, as in time is up

explanation.surface: An Association football game has finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Association football' reads as soccer, but 'Association' is the definition and 'football match' a cup tie.
explanation.definitionFit: A tie-up is a link or partnership between organisations.

clue.text: Spell a word

definitions.meaning: a period of time, as in a school or prison stint
a word or expression, especially a technical one

explanation.definitionFit: A term is a fixed period, a spell, and also a word used for a concept.

clue.text: See beyond river bank

indicators.note: beyond means following on after, so the see comes after the river's letter

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city and bishop's see in Cambridgeshire

explanation.surface: Look past the riverbank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bank' is a verb, as in banking on someone. A see is a bishop's diocese; Ely is a famous English one.
explanation.definitionFit: To bank on someone is to rely on or count on them.
